title: Speaking the Truth in Love
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Speaking the truth in love means using words faithfully, humbly, and courageously for the good of others before God. Biblical love does not hide truth, and biblical truth must not be spoken with cruelty, pride, or selfishness.
summary: Speaking the truth in love means using words faithfully, humbly, and courageously for the good of others before God. Biblical love does not hide truth, and biblical truth must not be spoken with cruelty, pride, or selfishness.
christFocus: Jesus Christ perfectly speaks truth with grace. He exposes sin, calls people to repentance, comforts the broken, confronts hypocrisy, and reveals the Father without deceit, cowardice, harshness, or selfish ambition.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God calls His people to speak truthfully. Lies, flattery, manipulation, gossip, exaggeration, and cowardly silence do not reflect the character of Christ. Truth matters because God is true and His people are called to walk in the light.

But truth must be spoken in love. Some people use truth as a weapon to shame, dominate, win arguments, or display superiority. Scripture does not permit harshness to masquerade as faithfulness.

Speaking truth in love requires wisdom. There is a time to speak, a way to speak, and a heart posture that matters. Correction should be humble, encouragement sincere, warning sober, and comfort tender.

This doctrine shapes relationships in the church, family, friendship, discipleship, correction, and conflict. God’s people are called to put away falsehood and speak truth as members of one another, building up rather than tearing down.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many relationships are damaged by either brutal honesty without love or false peace without truth. Some people avoid hard conversations because they fear rejection. Others speak harshly and claim they are “just telling the truth.” Both can harm souls.

This doctrine gives a better way. Truth and love belong together because Christ is full of grace and truth. God’s people should be safe enough to tell the truth and loving enough to speak it with humility, patience, and care.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Before you speak, ask whether your words are true, necessary, loving, humble, and aimed at building up. Refuse gossip, manipulation, cowardly silence, and harsh correction. Let Christ govern your mouth so your words bring light, repentance, courage, healing, and wisdom rather than confusion or harm.
